reason: NCC_EXTP003] Instructions generated by compiler 2064384 exceeds the typical limit of 150000. Input computation graph is too big due to large operators - Consider

evidence.verdict: compiler_instructions is NOT a measurement of this graph. It is invariant.
how_settled: The operator the compiler rejects is a flash-attention backward kernel, and its tensor shape is printed in the error context. dy_ref is (2,16,128,4096) / (4,...) / (8,...) at micro-batch 2/4/8 -- a 4x range in the volume of the very operator being complained about, 16.8M -> 67.1M elements.
All three rungs, plus this lane at micro-batch 2 with gradient checkpointing OFF (a lever no rung varied), report bit-identical 2064384.
Every rung compiled fresh: each emitted its own distinct MODULE_ hash and its own 'Failed compilation with [neuronx-cc...]' subprocess invocation. Cache replay is ruled out independently of the flag.

Across the entire study there are 59 occurrences of 'Instructions generated by compiler' in 10 lane logs over 3 independent runs (2026-08-05, 08-06, 08-12) and two compiler-flag hashes. All 59 read 2064384. No configuration anywhere produces a different value.
An instruction count cannot be invariant to a 4x change in the volume of the operator that triggered the error. Therefore the number does not describe these graphs.
evidence.consequence: The batch-ladder audit heuristic -- 'identical counts across failed rungs means the rungs reused a cached failure' -- is UNSOUND. Identical counts are what independently-compiled, genuinely-different graphs produce here. The sound audit signal is the per-rung MODULE_ hash plus a fresh neuronx-cc invocation, both of which are already in the logs.
evidence.still_unknown: What 2064384 actually denotes. Its shape (63 * 2^15, i.e. 2016 * 1024) suggests a fixed capacity or sentinel rather than a count. Settling that needs neuronx-cc internals, not another lane.
evidence.note: These fields were derived POST-HOC from lane logs, not written by the lane.
